items.title: Marian McPartland — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The one I was closest to was Uncle Cyril... He and his wife Sylvia came to New York and saw me at the Hickory House... He thought the Hickory House was just a terrible place for me to be in. He sat through one set, and then he said to me, 'Margaret, does your father know what you’re doing?'

ctx.x: Sounds like we’ve covered most of . . . what about one other question. On your mother’s side, does she have siblings?

Oh yes, my mother had a brother, Arthur. He was married. I remember them in my childhood. He had a . . . his wife was named Amy, but I don’t think they had any children. There’s a lot of assorted cousins and second cousins still roaming around in Windsor, but I lost touch. The one I was closest to was Uncle Cyril, who was knighted. We always called him “Uncle.” He wasn’t really my uncle. He and his wife Sylvia came to New York and saw me at the Hickory House. They were having a convention of mayors in Windsor,…

I was going to ask you, just as a followup. This is kind of getting into some of your early and fond memories in life socially in Windsor, and how did that cultivate your interest in music? But you stated a little earlier about one of your relatives, uncles I think, played cello, and someone else played. Did any . . . did your parents directly, either one of them, are involved with playing a musical instrument or singing?
